Subject: FinCo evaluation — next steps (model fit & evals)

Jason / Priya — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a mutual action plan:

Call recap:
- Goal: validate model fit for FinCo's customer support summarization + answer synthesis workflow (sensitive PII occasionally present).
- Success criteria (high-level): >=88% accuracy on labeled test set, low hallucination rate (<5% severe), and no critical safety failures on targeted prompts.

Recommended quick baseline models to evaluate (we'll run these on Redwood's eval runner):
- Redwood-7B-q4 (fast, cost-effective baseline)
- Llama2-13B-ptq (strong quality baseline)
- Mistral-7B (optional higher-quality check)

Benchmark & prompt material:
- Redwood benchmark report (attached) — shows prior results on similar extraction/summarization workloads.
- Prompt set + examples: https://drive.google.com/finco-test-prompts (shared)

Dataset / format we need you to upload:
- CSV: columns = id, input, expected, category, sensitive_flag
- Max rows for initial run: 2k (we can scale after baseline)
- Please redact or mark PII in "sensitive_flag" if you cannot share raw values. If you want, we can run on a private deployment or use customer-managed KMS for extra controls.

Scoring & evaluation plan (high-level):
- Automated: exact-match / token-F1 for extraction, ROUGE/EM for summaries.
- Safety / hallucination: automated classifier + manual spot checks.
- Human eval: 100-sample rubric for response usefulness and hallucination severity.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You upload finco_eval_dataset.csv to the shared eval workspace (link below) — target: EOD Wed 2/25.
2) Redwood provisions eval workspace and seeds prompts / scoring templates — ETA 24 hours after upload.
3) Baseline run: Redwood-7B-q4 + Llama2-13B-ptq — results in ~48 hours after run starts.
4) Review results together and decide on quantization/latency trade-offs.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft MAP)

Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if you'd like a step-by-step walk-through.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: FinCo evaluation — next steps (model fit & evals)

Jason — thanks for the quick reply and the sample CSV. Answers and proposed adjustments below.

1) PII / data controls:
- Hosted eval workspace: data is encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed KMS by default. For extra control we can:
  • Use customer-managed KMS (we'll record the key usage in audit logs)
  • Run the eval on your Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC) so raw data never leaves your environment.
- If you need us to, we can also run a redaction pass (hash/replace) on the PII columns before any model sees the text; please indicate in the CSV (sensitive_flag = true).

2) Scoring weights & initial smoke test:
- We can absolutely adopt your suggested weighting for the first acceptance pass: 40% safety/hallucination, 40% accuracy (EM/F1), 20% human eval. We'll reflect that in the scoring config.
- We'll run a 200-row smoke test first to sanity-check pipeline, then the full 2k baseline. Smoke test ETA: within 24 hours of your confirmation.

3) Dataset format & prompts (detailed):
- Required CSV columns: id | input | expected | category | sensitive_flag
  • id: unique string
  • input: customer support thread text (plain text)
  • expected: reference summary/answer (plain text)
  • category: e.g., "billing", "technical", "compliance" (helps stratified sampling)
  • sensitive_flag: true|false (if true, indicate redact or request private run)
- Prompt set: place examples in the Drive link and include 5 golden examples per category for human eval. Provide any special scoring policies in a separate doc if you have them.

4) How to run eval on Redwood (UI + CLI highlights):
- UI: go to https://redwood.app/evals/FINCO-042 -> New Eval -> Upload CSV -> Select models (Redwood-7B-q4, Llama2-13B-ptq) -> Choose scoring functions (exact_match, token_f1, safety_classifier) -> Set weights (40 safety / 40 accuracy / 20 human) -> Start run.
- CLI (example):
  redwood eval create --workspace FINCO-042 --dataset finco_eval_dataset.csv --models redwood-7b-q4,llama2-13b-ptq --scorers exact_match,token_f1,safety_classifier --weights 0.4,0.4,0.2

5) Baseline configuration suggestions:
- Run both models at default temperature (0.0-0.2) for deterministic outputs for extraction tasks.
- For summarization, run with temperature 0.2 and max_tokens tuned to expected length.
- Enable prefix caching where possible to speed repeated prompt runs.

Next steps (proposed):
- We will run the 200-row smoke test as soon as you confirm the sample above (we have the attached CSV).
- After smoke passes, we'll run the 2k baseline and share the benchmark report + a short action recommendation (quantize vs larger model tradeoffs).

Attached: redwood_benchmark_report.pdf (prior similar workloads)

Best,
Marissa
